A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same instruction-vector study. Their main texts, equations, figures, tables and appendices are readable and can be matched despite the expanded material in v2.

before.justification: v1 reports original OLMo activation-patching experiments, task accuracies, representation analyses and attention-path measurements in Sections 3–6 and Appendices A–D.

after.justification: v2 retains these empirical results and adds three-layer patching results, path-selection sensitivity analyses and statistical analyses of attention-head activity.

M1.justification: v1 restricts path tracing to maximum-attention edges. v2 additionally enumerates top-k edges, including k=2 and k=3, generalizing this selection procedure (Section 6.1; Appendices E–F). The activation-patching method and locally linear decomposition remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same four contrastive tasks and four BigBench tasks listed in Table 1. Additional accuracy entries and path analyses concern this existing coverage.

E2.justification: The existing comparisons retain the OLMo-2 base, SFT and DPO checkpoints. No competing interpretability method is added or removed from an evaluated comparison. The removed OLMo-3 runtime column had no corresponding baseline-result comparison.

E3.justification: v2 adds three-layer patching configurations and k=2/3 path-analysis settings, with Spearman correlations, Jaccard comparisons and an active-head threshold of 0.1. Section 3 also revises the reported checkpoint lineage from separate SFT/DPO training to base-to-SFT-to-DPO progression; this does not establish that existing experiments were rerun. Sample-count correspondence between Table 4 and the head-analysis descriptions remains unclear.

E4.justification: Section 6.1 and new Appendices E–F substantially extend the earlier qualitative head-pattern analysis. They test sensitivity to k, compare activity across tasks and neighboring token positions, assess activity against noise, and connect active layers to three-layer patching results. The additional unnormalized heatmaps redisplay existing data and are not separate robustness experiments.

E5.justification: Beyond the retained superadditivity t-tests, v2 introduces head-activity confidence intervals using 10,000 bootstrap resamples, tests described as comparing activity against Gaussian noise, and raw p-value visualizations (Section 6.1; Appendix F). These substantially expand uncertainty reporting without establishing additional independent model runs.

E6.justification: v1 Tables 3–14 retain their values as v2 Tables 5–16. v2 adds three-layer contributions (Tables 17–18), head correlations and similarities, k-dependent path findings, and BigBench accuracy entries in Figure 20. For example, Table 18 newly reports a 0.14 rank contribution for SFT antonym patching at layers (3,14,15), a new configuration rather than a same-setting performance gain.

T1.justification: The Transformer formalism, superadditivity inequality and locally linear derivation in Equations 1–3 are retained. No new theorem, proof or substantive mathematical derivation is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the central claims: instruction representations form eagerly, are linearly separable yet interact superadditively, and act as circuit selectors investigated through locally linear path tracing. The additional evidence does not redefine these contributions.

C2.justification: v2 develops interpretations of post-training as refining existing representations, head-pattern stability across k, and connections between active heads and patching triples. Appendix E discusses the antonym task's earlier-token exception. The limitations substantially expand to address simple instructions, syntactically separated instructions and queries, and missing intermediate training checkpoints.

D1.justification: Appendix A adds k-specific runtimes and sample counts, notes longer SFT/DPO runtimes, and removes the OLMo-3 runtime column. The listed code repository changes from arxiv2026-instruction-vectors to acl2026-instruction-vectors. Hardware and non-quantized model disclosures remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds Wu et al. (2024) and Heo et al. (2024) on instruction-following behavior and representations, plus Biderman et al. (2023) as a possible route to studying intermediate checkpoints. The broader positioning against existing representation and circuit-discovery approaches remains.

P1.justification: The revision makes localized wording changes and expands Sections 5–6 and the limitations while retaining the main narrative and section sequence. Superadditivity-test details move to Appendix B, and new Appendices E–F organize the added analyses.

P2.justification: v2 substantially expands the displays with correlation and similarity tables, three-layer result tables, and statistical heatmaps. Figures 12–19 add differently scaled views of existing patching data. Figure 4 gains total-path reference bars, and the accuracy plot becomes a wider eight-task display with reordered checkpoint labels.

improvement.justification: v2 strengthens the earlier reliance on one path-selection setting and qualitative head maps through sensitivity checks, quantitative comparisons and uncertainty reporting. It also clarifies checkpoint progression and applicability limits. However, Table 4 lists 20/15 samples for k=2/3 while head-analysis passages and captions report 100 without clearly reconciling the counts. These reporting ambiguities limit reproducibility and the strength of the overall gain.
